chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid narrated from Abī Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said, “Teach me something, O Messenger of Allah.” He عليه السلام said: “Hold fast to despairing of what is in the hands of people, for that is present wealth.” He said, “Increase me, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Beware of greed, for it is present poverty.” He said, “Increase me, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When you intend an affair, then reflect upon its outcome. If it is good or right guidance, follow it; and if it is evil or error, leave it.”

key_terms.الطَّمَعَ: Greed or covetous desire for what others have.
key_terms.الْغِنَى الْحَاضِرُ: Immediate richness; a present state of inner sufficiency.
key_terms.الْفَقْرُ الْحَاضِرُ: Immediate poverty; an inward state of neediness caused by greed.
key_terms.الْيَأْسِ مِمَّا فِي أَيْدِي النَّاسِ: Giving up hope in what people possess; detachment from dependence on others.
key_terms.رُشْداً: Right guidance and soundness in conduct.

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله teach about greed, contentment, and thinking about consequences?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches detachment from what others possess, warning that freedom from coveting people’s wealth is a form of immediate richness, while greed is a form of immediate poverty. It also instructs a believer to reflect on the consequences of any intended action, following what leads to good and right guidance and abandoning what leads to evil and misguidance.
